[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]HOW A TOWN DIES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Through the 2030s and 2040s the megacorps invested only in the cities they controlled: jobs, technology, hospitals, schools and private security were there and nowhere else. In small and medium towns the administrations were dismantled, local businesses were bought and closed, natural resources were fenced off, and advertising painted life outside the metropolises as backwardness. The towns died one by one.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE BUYER[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Whoever bought the land of the dead towns, demolished what was left and sold it back to the megacorps was almost always [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF][b]Portenova Corp[/b][/color][/url][color=white]. While [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2557482][color=#7FDBFF]Manuella Portenova[/color][/url][color=white] handed out cheap houses in front of the cameras, she decided far from them where Los Vales would live and where it would stop existing.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE SUSPICION[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The most suspicious say some disasters were caused on purpose to push people out — fires, contaminated wells, roads left to collapse. Nothing was ever proven. The Great Fire of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]La Maria[/color][/url][color=white] in 2039 is the case people cite most, because Portenova bought the ashes.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE EXODUS[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Between 2030 and 2050 about 1,200 towns died and some 41 million people moved. Few of them chose where to go. A town lost its hospital, then its school, then its water, and the families followed the last bus to whichever city was hiring that year. The Monopolization was only the largest of the great movements that made Los Vales.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE GHOST CITIES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Most dead towns were demolished and sold. A few were not: nobody bought them, or the price of the ruins was higher than the price of the land. Four ghost cities still stand in Los Vales. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Valewood[/color][/url][color=white] rents them as film sets; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Thirsty[/color][/url][color=white] Ones and the Unregistered live in them; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Lockwell[/color][/url][color=white] uses one as a camp.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE DEAD ROAD[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Before [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Zyxtopia[/color][/url][color=white] there was a shorter way. [/color][color=white][b]Route 12[/b][/color][color=white] opened in 1979 as a two-lane road straight across the desert from La Maria to the Taggarela river, where the motels of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69[/color][/url][color=white] stood. When the refugees of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832719][color=#7FDBFF]Hermosa[/color][/url][color=white] turned those motels into [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Las Dulces[/color][/url][color=white], Route 12 became its back door: 310 km of asphalt, three gas stations, two towns and no police. Smoke went down it from La Maria and money came back up.[/color]

[color=white]In 2042, with the walls of Zyxtopia half built, the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999866][color=#7FDBFF]Cabinet[/color][/url][color=white] "retired" Route 12. Portenova bought the bridge over the Taggarela and took it apart for steel, and from then on every trip between La Maria and Las Dulces went through the new capital and its tolls — 520 km instead of 310. In three years both towns on the road were empty; their people walked to the builders’ camp outside Zyxtopia, and are part of the reason the Favela grew so fast.[/color]

[color=white]Valians call it the [/color][color=white][b]Dead Road[/b][/color][color=white]. Sand covers half of it, and no map of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Trans Vales[/color][/url][color=white] shows it. It is the most used road in Los Vales that does not exist: the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832717][color=#7FDBFF]Golden Mafia[/color][/url][color=white] runs contraband down it with no tolls and no cameras, the Thirsty Ones hide water trucks in the old gas stations, and in 2088 the illegal [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69 Race[/color][/url][color=white] ran its last stage on it, to the river where there is no longer a bridge.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE FAVELA[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Illuminated Favela[/color][/url][color=white] is older than the city it lights. Zyxtopia opened as the capital in 2046, but its walls began to rise in 2038, on the site of an old [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Nakama State[/color][/url][color=white] town. Eight years of building needed hundreds of thousands of hands, and the workers lived where they could: in a camp outside the wall they were building. By 2046 about 400,000 people lived there. Nobody sent them away when the work was done.[/color]

[color=white]The camp kept growing. The last families of the dead towns of the Nakama State had nowhere else to go, and by 2049 about 1.3 million people lived against the wall — which is why the Union’s Operation Favela Line could kill 540,000 of them that June. The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2834884][color=#7FDBFF]Rebirth Plan[/color][/url][color=white] rebuilt Valewood and Route 69. It rebuilt nothing in the Favela, and the Favela rebuilt itself. Nobody counts it now; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Beacons[/color][/url][color=white], who sell it its light, think it holds about four million people.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]SEVEN CITIES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]What remains are the seven metropolises — [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Ferox[/color][/url][color=white], [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832735][color=#7FDBFF]Universalia[/color][/url][color=white], La Maria, Zyxtopia, Las Dulces, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Las Noites[/color][/url][color=white] and Valewood — each one, in practice, the property of the corporations. Those who did not fit went to the [/color][color=white][b]Illuminated Favela[/b][/color][color=white] outside Zyxtopia’s walls, or to the abandoned villages of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Escaldar[/color][/url][color=white], where the Thirsty Ones still bring water.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]
